greek_edition: Lagarde 1858, Hippolyti Romani quae feruntur omnia graece (text-layer copy hippolytiromani00hippgoog_text.pdf); printed page = PDF page minus 21; OCR text layer; Migne PG 10 col. 815 OCR agrees
english: Let him attend to the fact, and understand that He did not say, "I and the Father am one, but are one." For the word are is not said of one person, but it refers to two persons, and one power.
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 226 (ch. 7); Lagarde printed p. 49
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 5 (Roberts-Donaldson, 1885 Buffalo/Edinburgh; archive.org antenicenefather05robeuoft), OCR djvu text; printed page from OCR page markers
what_it_says: Christ said 'we are one' (ἕν, neuter), not 'I am one'; the word refers to two persons and one power.
limits: Greek ch. 7 and 'ἓν ἐσμεν' (neuter) are read from OCR; ANF translation is 'are one'. Jn 10:30 is cited as the Johannine saying; Lagarde's ch. 7 uses Jn 17:22 for the 'one' prayer. Does not show the Son as ontologically equal; only shows a 'two persons, one power' concept.

ref: Contra Noetum ch. 9-10 (Lagarde PDF pp. 71-72 = printed 50-51; ANF vol. 5 pp. 227)
greek: θεὸς μόνος ὑπάρχων καὶ μηδὲν ἔχων ἑαυτῷ σύγχρονον, ἐβουλήθη κόσμον κτίσαι
greek_edition: Lagarde 1858, Hippolyti Romani quae feruntur omnia graece (text-layer copy hippolytiromani00hippgoog_text.pdf); printed page = PDF page minus 21; OCR text layer; 'φῶς ἐκ φωτὸς γεννῶν προῆκεν' is on PDF p. 72 (ch. 10 per Lagarde)
english: 10. God, subsisting alone, and having nothing contemporaneous with Himself, determined to create the world. ... uttering the voice first, and begetting Him as Light of Light, He set Him forth to the world as its Lord, (and) His own mind (ANF ch. 10).
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 227 (ch. 10); Lagarde printed p. 50-51
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 5 (Roberts-Donaldson, 1885 Buffalo/Edinburgh; archive.org antenicenefather05robeuoft), OCR djvu text; printed page from OCR page markers
what_it_says: Before creation God is alone; the Word is begotten as Light of Light and sent forth to the world.
limits: Ch. 10 is a 'Logos before the world' model (Logos as manifested Word and 'power' of the Father). It uses 'Light of Light' but in the economic/manifestation sense; no homoousios. Subordinationist readers cite 'set forth' and 'manifested'.

ref: Contra Noetum ch. 14 (Lagarde PDF pp. 73-74 = printed 52-53; Migne PG 10 col. 823; ANF vol. 5 p. 228; ANCL 9 PDF p. 72)
greek: δύο μὲν οὐκ ἐρῶ θεοὺς, ἀλλ᾽ ἢ ἕνα, πρόσωπα δὲ δύο, οἰκονομίαν δὲ τρίτην τὴν χάριν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. πατὴρ μὲν γὰρ εἷς, πρόσωπα δὲ δύο, ὅτι καὶ ὁ υἱός, τὸ δὲ τρίτον τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα
greek_edition: Lagarde 1858, Hippolyti Romani quae feruntur omnia graece (text-layer copy hippolytiromani00hippgoog_text.pdf); printed page = PDF page minus 21; OCR text layer; Lagarde OCR reads οἰκονομίῳ in the text, footnote lists variants; Migne PG 10 col. 823 OCR agrees (Πατὴρ μὲν γὰρ εἷς, Πρόσωπα δὲ δύο, ὅτι καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς, τὸ δὲ τρίτον τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα)
english: I shall not indeed speak of two Gods, but of one; of two Persons however, and of a third economy (disposition), viz., the grace of the Holy Ghost. For the Father indeed is One, but there are two Persons, because there is also the Son; and then there is the third, the Holy Spirit.
translator: S. D. F. Salmond (ANF vol. 5); ANCL 9 (MacMahon/Salmond, 1868) same wording on PDF p. 72
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 228 (ch. 14); Lagarde printed p. 52
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 5 (Roberts-Donaldson, 1885 Buffalo/Edinburgh; archive.org antenicenefather05robeuoft), OCR djvu text; printed page from OCR page markers; ANCL vol. 9 (1868) PDF p. 72
what_it_says: 'The Father is one, but there are two Persons, because there is also the Son, and the third is the Holy Spirit'; one God, three named persons in economy.
limits: Here 'persons' (prosopa) means economic/manifested persons; ANF footnote (editorial, not Hippolytus) reads it as 'one God, three Persons'. Nicene 'one ousia' is not stated in this passage. The brief's 'C. Noet. 14' is correct; the 'Father commands' sentence is also ch. 14, not 12-13.

ref: Contra Noetum ch. 14, second half (Lagarde PDF p. 74 = printed 53; Migne PG 10 col. 823)
greek: ὁ γὰρ κελεύων πατήρ, ὁ δὲ ὑπακούων υἱός, τὸ δὲ συνετίζον ἅγιον πνεῦμα. ὁ ὢν πατὴρ ἐπὶ πάντων, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς διὰ πάντων, τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἐν πᾶσιν
greek_edition: Lagarde 1858, Hippolyti Romani quae feruntur omnia graece (text-layer copy hippolytiromani00hippgoog_text.pdf); printed page = PDF page minus 21; OCR text layer; Migne PG 10 col. 823 OCR reads 'Πατὴρ ἐντέλλεται, Λόγος ἀποτελεῖ, Υἱὸς δὲ δείκνυται ... ὁ ὧν Πατὴρ ἐπὶ πάντων'
english: It is the Father who commands, and the Son who obeys, and the Holy Ghost who gives understanding: the Father who is above all, and the Son who is through all, and the Holy Spirit who is in all.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 5 (Roberts-Donaldson, 1885 Buffalo/Edinburgh; archive.org antenicenefather05robeuoft), OCR djvu text; printed page from OCR page markers
what_it_says: The Father commands, the Son obeys, the Spirit gives understanding; Father above all, Son through all, Spirit in all.
limits: Ordering language ('the Father commands', 'the Son obeys') is the basis of subordinationist readings; the same text says the Father is above all and the Spirit in all. OCR of 'ὑπακούων' and 'δείκνυται' is not perfect in Lagarde (read 'δεβινυται').
